pull_request.title: Infrastructure: add interaction statistics and message colors to Pages
pull_request.head: codex/interaction-statistics
pull_request.body:
The merged interaction records could be browsed per PR but had no project-wide counts. Add a **Statistics** tab to the existing GitHub Pages resource ledger, with source breakdowns, definitions, coverage and a downloadable aggregate JSON report. It updates automatically in the existing Pages build after merge.

Human-associated comments, prompts, responses and reviews use blue; agent-associated messages use orange. Participant cards, avatars, sender names and message borders follow the same palette. A visible legend and existing identity labels retain the distinction without color alone. Publishing accounts and unrecorded identities remain neutral gray.

At main revision `78bef505c4e623739da204ce92e3aa7bc6f931c5`, the retained evidence contains:

| Measure | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Human words | 15,132 |
| Agent response words | 205,404 |
| Publishing-account response words | 71,615 |
| Combined response words | 277,019 |
| Unique recorded-message / GitHub discussion and review events | 3,077 |
| Canonical bounded task sessions | 304 |
| Tracked scientific tasks (separate registry) | 111 |
| PR records | 123 |
| Named human accounts | 7 |
| Exposed agent threads (instance proxy) | 134 |
| Retained visible-turn snapshots | 522 |
| Exposed tool-operation calls | 24,355 |

These are baseline counts before this PR's own session and interaction record are added. Named accounts do not establish distinct people; unnamed local speakers remain unidentified. Thread IDs are the available proxy for agent instances, without inferring physical processes.

The counter validates source ledgers and deduplicates stable message IDs, event URLs, account turns and thread identities across PR/fork references. Agent handoffs, unresolved authorship, journal excerpts and other curated records have separate subtotals. Uploads, generated outcome references and bodyless review-state labels do not add authored words. Journal call aggregates are not added to exposed per-turn operations. Evidence is what is retained in Git, including stale open/closed snapshots and explicit pinned branch references; no live/private-client collection or current merge-status inference is introduced.

Validation: 28 token-site tests (including eight counting/publication controls), 19 interaction-ledger tests, both existing Node suites, canonical session/interaction/token validators, deterministic site/output controls, complete Pages build and whitespace checks passed. Localhost preview returned HTTP 200. Browser visual QA was unavailable because the computer-use service had no accessible browser window.

Infrastructure only: no scientific progress entry, geometry change, token estimate, historical usage reassignment or design sign-off.

events.text:
An independent extraction of the tracked evidence at the starting main revision
gave 15,132 human words; 205,404 agent response words and 71,615 publishing-account
response words (277,019 combined); 3,077 message/discussion/review events; 304
canonical bounded sessions (299 closed, 5 open); 111 scientific registry tasks;
123 PR records; 7 named human accounts plus unnamed local speakers; 134 exposed
agent threads; 589 canonical usage turns; 522 retained visible-turn snapshots;
and 24,355 exposed operation calls. This task's new session and PR subsequently
increase the live source-revision counts, so these baseline numbers are not
hard-coded into the site.

The initial human subtotal of 15,193 included 61 bodyless review-state labels.
These labels are metadata rather than authored text; their events remain counted
but their words are excluded. A regression covers the correction. Seven inherited
messages disagree on human/agent authorship and remain unresolved.

The count covers all evidence retained on main, including dated snapshots whose
PR state may be stale and explicitly pinned branch-only references. No live merge
status is inferred. Numbers/code/URL components count literally; upload events and
generated references add no words. Named accounts do not establish distinct people.
Threads are the instance proxy; sessions, role assignments and physical processes
are not interchangeable. Tool metadata is deduplicated by turn without adding
journal aggregates or assuming wrapper calls equal individual program executions.

coverage.prompts: Available account-matched user-visible messages, public Codex inputs and curated journal excerpts. Historical full input coverage is unknown.
coverage.responses: Public responses and recorded outcomes; no private model state or hidden reasoning.
coverage.token_accounting: References only. Never sum accounts across PRs or assign a shared turn by text length.
coverage.unknowns: Unrecorded names, models, tools, subagent identities and response links remain unknown; empty lists are not zero activity.
coverage.remote: Snapshot, not live synchronization; deleted/edited history and emoji reactions are not recovered.
coverage.branch_only: Pinned branch journal snapshots are references, not imported counters. Unretained or other-device inputs remain unknown.
